collection_method: Amazon Seller Forums, Account Health category, fetched logged out. sellercentral.amazon.com/robots.txt was re-fetched immediately before collection and allows /seller-forums by explicit allowlist entry while carrying a broad Disallow: / otherwise; /forums/search and /forums/search.jspa are explicitly disallowed and are hard-blocked in code, not by convention.

standards.never_quoted: No forum post text is reproduced anywhere in these records. Every string in `observation` is our own structural description.
standards.never_a_policy_fact: A forum post is evidence of what a seller says happened. Policy facts come from Tier A/B/D sources only.
standards.never_in_a_denominator: These records live in seed_observation, never outcome_record.
standards.never_counted: contributes_to_supporting_n is 0 for every record, by schema const. Gate G16.
standards.thread_dates_are_inferences: Forum pages render relative dates ('2 days ago'). Absolute dates below are inferences from the retrieval date and are labelled as such.

coverage_note: Two seeds, both on AMZ.OPS.VERIFICATION, because that is what the Account Health category surfaced on the day of collection. This is a thin, non-representative sample and is recorded as such — CORPUS_DESIGN.md §4.5 is explicit that the seed is the weakest material in the system and is scaffolding, not a moat. It is deliberately not padded out: a fabricated post-mortem would be worse than a small one.

observations.source_surface: Amazon Seller Forums — Account Health category
observations.thread_date_note: Thread renders as roughly four weeks old at retrieval, with replies continuing for about three weeks after the opening post. Absolute dates are an inference, not a stated fact.

observation.enforcement_action: A wave of identity and bank-account verification demands tied to annual INFORM Act compliance, with an at-risk-of-deactivation warning shown on the account dashboard.
what_the_seller_submitted: Government photo identification, front and back
A credit card or financial statement
In some cases a business registration extract
structural_notes: Multiple participants describe an expired identity document as the trigger, not a missing one — the document existed and had lapsed.
Several describe receiving contradictory automated messages, one reporting verification failure and one reporting approval, within the same episode.
The dashboard at-risk warning is described as persisting after the seller believed the submission was complete, which is what drove the forum post rather than the verification itself.
Processing is described as taking substantially longer than participants expected for straightforward documentation.

observations.what_it_shaped: The mandatory-evidence note that the requested document must be in date and unaltered, and the preventive requirement of a named owner for document expiry dates. A hypothesis about where this code fails, not evidence that it does.

observations.source_surface: Amazon Seller Forums — Account Health category
observations.thread_date_note: Thread renders as two days old at retrieval with a reply one day old. Absolute dating is an inference.

observation.enforcement_action: Account locked by an automated verification process over a mismatch between the registered business type and the document submitted — the account was registered as an individual and a business licence was supplied.
what_the_seller_submitted: A business licence for INFORM Act verification
Corporate bank account documentation, including confirmation of the platform's own test deposit
A prior support email from an earlier year approving the use of business documentation
structural_notes: The defect is a mismatch between account registration and document, not an absence of documentation — the seller had documents, of the wrong type for the registration.
The seller's argument is a history-of-compliance argument, asking for manual review rather than an exception.
The case is described as escalated by a support specialist and then closed by an automated rejection, with the escalation not visibly reaching a decision.
The remedy the seller asks for is a correction to the platform's own registration data, which is a different request from an appeal against a finding.

observations.what_it_shaped: AP.ENTITY_MISMATCH and AP.SUBSTITUTE_DOCUMENT in the L3 pattern, and the must_contain item requiring the mismatch to be named before the reviewer finds it. Again: a hypothesis to test against the golden set, not a finding.
